_comment: Thresholds for the engine-to-founder translation layer (backend/founder_view.py).
They live in a data file rather than in either implementation because the
client is local-first: Home computes runway and unit economics from numbers
the browser holds and never sends, so those few rules exist on both sides.
frontend/src/founderView.js imports this file directly (Vite resolves JSON),
so neither side carries its own copy of a number.
_rule_of_40_mrr_floor_why: Rule of 40 is a public-SaaS benchmark and is meaningless below roughly $1M ARR. 83,333 is $1M/12. Below it the spend-per-revenue-dollar ratio is shown instead.
_ltv_cac_healthy_why: The engine's own threshold in compute_reward: below 3x it penalises the policy.
_ltv_cac_unmeasurable_why: Above this the ratio is measurement noise, not health. A founder who spent $10 and signed 10 customers has a $1 CAC and a 100x ratio; printing 'Healthy' for that is worse than printing nothing.
_cac_min_customers_why: New customers in the reported month below which a derived CAC is not reported at all.
_confidence_caps_why: Confidence used to be the model's own scalar, rendered beside the assumption count but computed independently of it, so the strip could read 'High confidence · 6 estimated inputs'. The count now caps the band, which makes that sentence impossible rather than merely unlikely.
